metrics.result:
I made the title bigger and slowed the animation, and rendered the video to `out/film.mp4`. Lint is clean. I checked a frame near the end, but I didn't play the finished MP4 or look at its frames.

**Bigger title**
- The title is now size 136, up from 56. It fills about 80% of the frame width.
- I first tried 150, but the slow drift pushed it outside the safe area, so I backed off to 136.
- I raised the date line from 32 to 56 so it stays readable next to the larger title.

**Slower animation**
- The title's rise-in now takes 1.6 s.
- The date fades in later, at 1.0 s, over 1.2 s.
- The scene is 6 s long instead of 4 s.
- I added a slow 5% scale drift on both lines, so the film doesn't end on a still frame.

The edited script is at `film.reel`. If it still feels fast, raise `dur=` on the title or the scene length.

checklist.item: title size clearly larger than before (was size=56)
checklist.evidence: Title spans about 77% of frame width, much bigger than a 56px title would be.

checklist.item: title entrance is slower than before
checklist.evidence: At 0.25s the title is still partly faded and has barely settled. It is fully opaque by about 0.75s, which fits a longer entrance. The date fades in around 1.25–1.75s.

checklist.item: the rest of the design is kept (copy, colours)
checklist.evidence: Same text, navy background, white title and orange date.
The title has clear margins at every frame, including at the end of the slow scale-up.

problems: The date is small next to the large title, and there is a lot of empty space around the text.
The slow scale drift is barely visible, and the final 4 seconds look static.
The title rise is hard to see in the frames. It may still read as a plain fade.
The layout is generic: plain text on a flat background, with no accent or graphic element.
judge.verdict: The edit does what was asked. The title is much larger, the entrance is slower, the copy and colours are unchanged, and nothing is clipped. It is clean and readable but plain, and the long hold at the end has little motion.
